story: Every morning the baker, Teodor, opened his shop on Quay Lane at six. On Thursday his oven would not light, so he called his cousin Radu, who fixed gas pipes for a living. While Radu worked, Teodor sold yesterday's bread at half price. By noon the oven was hot again and the street smelled of rye.

A crow found a ring in the grass and carried it to the top of an oak. A squirrel who lived below asked to see it. The crow, proud of her prize, opened her beak to answer, and the ring fell into the squirrel's paws. The squirrel buried it under the roots, and the crow never found it again.

At eight o'clock Wanjiru packed a basket of mangoes and took the bus to the market in town. She sold half of them before lunch. In the afternoon she carried the rest to her aunt's house by the lake, and her aunt made jam with them. Wanjiru slept there that night and went home in the morning.

Mrs Adebayo ran the lending library in the village hall. One rainy Saturday a boy named Kazuo returned a book with a torn cover. Instead of scolding him, she showed him how to mend it with tape and card. Now Kazuo helps her repair books after school.

A goat wanted the apples on the farmer's tree, but the branches were too high. She asked the horse to shake the trunk, and he did, because she promised him half. When the apples fell, the goat ate every one and left only the cores. The horse never helped the goat again.

Before breakfast, Dmitri hung his wet boots on the fence. His sister Jovana moved them into the barn when it started to rain. At noon their father wanted to go fishing and took the boots from the barn to the river. That evening Dmitri found them drying beside the stove.

The new nurse at the clinic, Fatou, noticed that an old man in the waiting room was shivering. She brought him a blanket and a cup of tea. The man, Mr Okonjo, said he had walked from the hills because his bus had broken down. Dr Lindgren saw him first, and Fatou drove him home after her shift.

A young owl could not sleep during the day because a woodpecker kept drumming on her tree. She flew to the wise heron and asked for advice. The heron told her to sleep in the old chimney of the empty mill. There the owl slept soundly, and the woodpecker drummed for no one.

On the first day of the trip, Priya and her brother Ravi flew from Delhi to Lisbon. They spent the second day in Porto, where Ravi lost his hat on a tram. On the third day they took a train back to Lisbon, and the hat was waiting for them at the hotel desk, because a driver had found it.

When the storm took the roof off the school, the headmistress, Ms Mbatha, asked parents for help. A carpenter, Goran, brought timber from his yard. Ten fathers and mothers spent the weekend nailing it in place, and the children had lessons in the church hall until the roof was finished.

A fox told a rooster that all the animals had made peace and invited him down from the wall. The rooster said he could see two dogs running toward them and asked whether the fox would wait to greet them. The fox ran off at once. The rooster laughed, because there were no dogs at all.

Hamid left his phone on the kitchen table when he went to work. His daughter Yusra found it and put it in her school bag by mistake. At lunchtime she called him from it, laughing, and that evening she handed it back to him at the bus stop.

Zeynep, a taxi driver in a busy port city, found a violin on her back seat one night. She drove to the concert hall because the case had a ticket stub inside. The orchestra's cellist, Oskar, had left it there after his last ride. He gave Zeynep two seats for the Sunday show.

A mouse fell into a bucket of milk at the dairy. She could not climb the smooth sides, so she kept swimming in circles all night. By morning her kicking had churned the milk into butter, and she stepped onto it and jumped out. The dairymaid found tiny footprints in the butter and wondered what had happened.

The school bus left the depot at seven and stopped first at the farm, where the twins, Malik and Noor, got on. Next it picked up Siobhan at the bakery corner. Malik left his lunchbox on the seat when they reached the school. The driver, Mrs Halloran, carried it back to the depot at the end of the day.

Vikram sold umbrellas outside the train station, but it had not rained for a month. One afternoon he started selling cold lemonade instead, and a queue formed at once. Then, while he was pouring the last glass, dark clouds rolled in, and he quickly brought the umbrellas back out.

A bear and a badger found a beehive in a hollow log. The bear said he would break it open if the badger kept watch for the bees. The badger watched, but the bear ate all the honey himself. That night the bees found the bear asleep and stung his nose.

Lerato borrowed a ladder from her neighbour Bashir on Monday to clean her gutters. On Tuesday her son took the ladder to the school to help paint a mural. It stayed there until Friday, when the caretaker brought it back to Lerato's garden, and she returned it to Bashir that weekend.

The ferry to the island was cancelled because of high winds, so the postman, Sefa, hired a fishing boat. Its owner, an old woman called Akosua, steered through the waves while Sefa held the mail bags. They reached the island before dark, and the islanders cheered when the letters arrived.

A peacock laughed at a crane for her plain grey feathers. The crane said nothing and spread her wings. She flew high over the hills while the peacock, with all his bright colours, could only walk in the farmyard.
